fields.value: Independent manuscript branches make interpolation costly when their separation predates the controversy that would motivate adding the resurrection list. If geographically separated witnesses already contain First Corinthians 15:3–11 before any coordinating authority could align them, the hypothesis must posit either repeated independent adoption or an insertion in an exceptionally early shared archetype. Those alternatives should then be tested against the persistence of other variants across the same branches. Agreement does not prove that no lost form ever existed, because surviving witnesses cannot reveal every stage of transmission. It does, however, shift the burden: interpolation must explain both the passage’s early distribution and the absence of a recoverable contrary stream.
